analysis.title: GS Basics - Fed. Hyperscalers. UK Budget. Cross-asset Sentiment
key_insights: SK Hynix reported a big beat overnight and the stock rose about 10%. Revenue was +32% sequentially, operating profit +38%, margins at 80%, and more than half of 2027/28 capacity is already under long term agreements. The semi tape is bid.

Financing concerns that hit the AI and semi complex are beginning to abate after a series of positive developments this week. The author says the demand side never changed. The debate was about supply, financing and a Street-wide risk reduction exercise.

The author says the selloff left some of the lowest net exposures of the year and among the largest two-week institutional tech liquidations on record. There were early signs of buying on 10/27, with people picking up parts of the semi complex and some demand for upside vol, but investors have barely begun to re-risk. The author describes what has happened so far as abatement of supply rather than meaningful fresh demand.

Fed: there are no projections at this meeting, so focus is on the vote, the statement and Warsh. A hold is fully priced. Two dissents is probably the central expectation, zero would be a dovish surprise and three would reinforce December as the next hike.

The author's guess is that the Fed tees up December without committing. The debate is how far the hiking cycle extends and how much the tightening in financial conditions offsets stubborn inflation. Rates have repriced materially, payroll growth is weak and housing is cooling, so there is room for a more balanced message. Watch the long end if the message sounds too soft on forward inflation. Little event risk is priced in equities.

Microsoft and Google earnings matter most today. The author puts buyside expectations at Azure growth in the high 40s% and Google Cloud in the mid 90s%. The question is whether results can beat already high expectations. Azure probably needs a guidance raise to be supportive.

If Microsoft or Google miss only because they cannot bring enough compute online, the author sees that as disappointing for near term revenue but potentially more bullish for the scarcity premium and future spending. Watch customer concentration, demand breadth, and the link between revenue growth, capex and margins.

UK Budget is today. Fiscal headroom is limited and the government needs new revenue. Possible measures are bank taxes, gambling levies, property measures and support for first time buyers. Banks are particularly sensitive. OBR forecasts and the gilt reaction probably matter as much as the headline measures.

Middle East: oil is bid again. Gulf equities rallied sharply on 10/27 on regional collective bargaining hopes, then opened lower after the WSJ reported Washington warned Gulf allies to prepare for a potentially short, aggressive campaign against Iran after the midterms. No final decision has been made. Israel's election looks deadlocked, with neither bloc holding a clear majority, so coalition uncertainty could last weeks.

Risk view: the author acknowledges headwinds (elevated energy, unresolved geopolitics, midterms next week) but says the market got extraordinarily pessimistic on AI and took nets too low. Confidence is low, positioning is light, the AI micro is improving and credit traded better on 10/27, which is the author's focal point. The author thinks gross can start working again in the right pockets of tech, still selectively, with a cleaner set-up into year end once the macro headwinds pass.
Side note: the Risk Appetite Indicator is below zero as tech dominates cross-asset moves.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler volumes in traffic, compute and infrastructure remain robust, which should lead to accelerating cloud growth, faster backlog conversion and stronger cash generation.
tension_points.bear_case: Expectations are already very high (Azure high 40s%, Google Cloud mid 90s%), and a miss from compute capacity limits would hurt near term revenue, with customer concentration and capex-to-margin economics under scrutiny.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Azure results without a guidance raise, or evidence that incremental economics from capex do not work.

tension_points.bull_case: Tighter financial conditions, repriced rates, weak payroll growth and cooling housing leave room for a more balanced Fed message.
tension_points.bear_case: Inflation is hot and stubborn, and three dissents would reinforce December as the next hike, with a soft message on forward inflation pressuring the long end.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Three dissents (reinforces a December hike) or a statement too soft on forward inflation that hits the long end.
